name: CHUHATSU North America, Inc.
old_description: CHUHATSU North America is proud to be part of Chuo Spring Co., LTD, a trusted global manufacturer of springs and control cables with over 75 years of innovation and excellence. Backed by decades of experience, we share in their enduring commitment to craftsmanship, creativity, and customer satisfaction. Together, we strive to meet the evolving needs of our industry while supporting a better, brighter future for our customers.
about:
CHUHATSU North America, Inc. operates a 300,000-square-foot facility in Glasgow, Kentucky. The company was formed in February 2017 through the merger of ACK (established 1989) and Chuo Precision Spring, becoming the North American arm of Chuo Spring Co., Ltd., a Japanese spring and control cable manufacturer founded in 1948.

The facility produces a range of automotive springs and control cables, including chassis springs, precision coil springs, flat springs, formed wire springs, leaf springs, torsion bars, torsion springs, snap rings, and spiral springs, as well as heavy-duty and light-duty control cables. Additional capabilities include stamping, e-coating, motor mount assembly, and stabilizer bar production. CHUHATSU serves as both a Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier to major automobile manufacturers.

Its customer base spans passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and ATVs and UTVs, with products designed for automotive OEM and Tier supplier programs from development through long-term production. The company emphasizes custom spring solutions tailored to specific vehicle platforms.

CHUHATSU’s corporate philosophy centers on enriching society through technology, pioneering the future with human wisdom, and challenging itself to fulfill every dream. Its stated objective is to design and manufacture the highest-quality products at competitive prices, provide superior service, meet delivery commitments, and employ qualified people with training opportunities. The company holds ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 certifications and has received the President’s Award from its parent company along with multiple customer delivery and performance awards.

name: CM Solutions, Inc.
old_description: CM Solutions is an innovative Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider that focuses on delivering complete end-to-end manufacturing capabilities with the latest technological solutions for companies.
about:
CM Solutions, Inc. was founded in 2002 in Corinth, Mississippi, as a privately owned contract manufacturer serving all electronics market segments. The company was established by Mike, Ron, Jack, and Tommy, who brought decades of combined experience in OEM and contract manufacturing both domestically and abroad. The founders remain actively involved in daily operations, maintaining a hands-on approach with customers.

The firm provides end-to-end electronic manufacturing services (EMS), including build-to-order (BTO), configure-to-order (CTO), and direct-ship programs that integrate seamlessly into customer supply chains. Over its history, CM Solutions has expanded its facility three times, growing to five production lines equipped with selective soldering, automatic optical inspection (AOI), multiple in-circuit test platforms, a DEK Horizon SMT printer, a Faraday cage for RF circuitry, and a dedicated conformal coating room. The company supports low-, medium-, and high-volume production with lead-free (RoHS-compliant) processes.

CM Solutions serves a range of industries, including automotive, medical, military, and general OEM markets. Its customer base spans domestic and international clients seeking customized manufacturing solutions for electronic assemblies. The company’s quality system aligns with IPC-A-610 Classes 1–3 and J-STD-001 standards, enabling it to meet the stringent requirements of regulated sectors.

The business was built on a customer-focused philosophy, emphasizing engineering capabilities, dedication to specific end markets, and technology advantages.

name: CMC Steel Alabama
old_description: At CMC, we’re proud of our heritage, but we’re even prouder of the innovative and pioneering spirit that has set us apart from our competitors and taken our mill operations and our products to new heights. Automation and environmentally friendly process advancements have revolutionized the way CMC makes steel.
about:
CMC Steel Alabama operates a steel mill in Birmingham, Alabama, as part of Commercial Metals Company (CMC), which emphasizes its heritage and innovative spirit in steelmaking. The facility uses electric arc furnace technology in a mini-mill configuration, with a melt capacity exceeding 5 million tons of finished long steel products annually. It produces a wide range of products including rebar, merchant bar, wire rod, and specialty engineered steels such as ChromX (corrosion-resistant reinforcing steel), GalvaBar (continuously galvanized rebar), CryoSteel (for cryogenic applications down to −274 °F), and Impact Metals (armor-grade steel). The mill also manufactures fence posts from 100% recycled U.S. billet steel and offers value-added processing like spooled and coiled rebar, structural shapes, and specialty bar items.

Its specialty products target marine infrastructure, defense and transportation OEMs, heavy equipment manufacturers, and LNG projects requiring cryogenic performance.

CMC differentiates itself through its low-carbon EAF steelmaking process, which it says produces 63% lower emissions intensity than the industry average, supplemented by renewable energy credits and carbon offsets. Proprietary product lines like ChromX and CryoSteel are designed to extend service life in harsh environments, while an integrated logistics network across multiple states supports reliable supply.

name: CRP Automotive
old_description: The Aftermarket Warehouse Distributors Association (AWDA) was founded in 1947 and is the oldest organized group of warehouse distributors and their respective suppliers of parts, accessories and other supplies for the motor vehicle aftermarket. AWDA’s 600+ members represent thousands of locations.
about:
CRP Automotive operates as a business unit of CRP Industries, a veteran-owned family business headquartered in Cranbury, New Jersey. Founded in 1954, the company began as a small importer offering roughly 200 sizes of German-manufactured tires to the North American market. Over more than 70 years of continuous operation, it has grown into an industry leader supplying thousands of automotive replacement parts and fluids across the continent. The privately held company spans three generations of family ownership and maintains additional facilities in South Carolina, Michigan, and Puebla, Mexico.

The company develops, manufactures, and distributes a broad portfolio of aftermarket products under brands that include AAE steering components, Rein Automotive parts, Pentosin technical fluids, and AJUSA gaskets and head bolts. Beyond new parts, CRP has extensive capabilities in mechanical and electronic remanufacturing, restoring components such as ABS modules, electronic power-steering modules, transmission control modules, instrument clusters, engine control modules, hybrid system inverters, and a range of other mechatronic units. Its product catalog, accessible via an online platform powered by ShowMeTheParts.com, covers nearly every automotive service and repair category for both import and domestic vehicles.

CRP Automotive serves the professional automotive repair market, working closely with technicians who select and install its products in shops across North America. The company also partners with major e-catalog platforms such as Activant/Epicor and WHI to ensure parts data reaches installers efficiently.

CRP states its purpose is to build a sustainable community where people and machines perform at their best, and its vision is to be the service-market partner that creates solutions for problems caused by advancing vehicle technology. The firm emphasizes its deep remanufacturing expertise and direct engagement with repair professionals as key differentiators that keep vehicles on the road longer and stronger.

name: CRS Hoods LLC - Restaurant Hood Installation
old_description: Your restaurant can’t open without a code-compliant hood system. Since 1980, We’ve installed 10,000+ commercial kitchen exhaust systems across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland—every one engineered to pass inspection the first time.
about:
CRS Hoods LLC operates from Smyrna, Delaware, tracing its roots to 1980 when Ron Grantland founded AG&G Sheet Metal, Inc. The family-owned business passed to his sons, Geoff and Andy, who worked alongside their father for decades.

The company designs, fabricates, and installs complete commercial kitchen ventilation systems. Its services cover Type I and Type II hood installation, exhaust fan installation and emergency repair, make-up air unit installation and balancing, welded grease duct fabrication, fire suppression integration, and ongoing repair, cleaning, and preventive maintenance. CRS Hoods serves Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland, with more than 10,000 systems installed since 1980. The team includes a CEO, vice president, and senior supervisor, supported by field technicians who schedule work around kitchen operations, including nights and early mornings.

Customers range from independent restaurants and fast-food chains to cafes, bakeries, bars, hotels, schools, hospitals, food trucks, ghost kitchens, and institutional cafeterias. The company also works on food hall projects and other multi-venue operations.

CRS Hoods emphasizes a "first-time pass" inspection record, built on three pillars: maintaining proper clearance from combustibles per NFPA 96, calculating make-up air to balance building pressure, and ensuring airstream integrity through liquid-tight external welds. It holds professional licenses in all four states it serves and promotes end-to-end service from on-site assessment and CAD-backed design through final inspection walkthrough.

about:
Cable Conveyor Systems Inc. was founded in 1975 in Columbia, South Carolina. President David M. Rauscher has been with the company since its inception and leads the business alongside Vice President Brooke Spence.

The company designs, manufactures, and installs custom cable conveyor systems for processors that move cans or plastic containers. Its product line includes cable can tracks, diverter gates, accessories, reconditioning parts, and bulk can cable, all built in aluminum or stainless steel. Cable Conveyor holds several national and international patents for its equipment, notably the Extruda-Mold® cable splicing system. Services span consulting, system design, on-site audits, and a portable splicing service that can be performed at a customer’s plant in about one hour.

Primary markets are food, dairy, beverage, motor oil, laundry soap, and pet food manufacturers—any operation that conveys cans or plastic containers. Customers range from new installations to existing lines needing integration, flow improvements, or production increases.

The firm emphasizes a full-service model: on-site audits deliver a photo‑documented report with a flat fee plus travel, and its patented Extruda-Mold splicing technique is guaranteed for two years on full can lines and four years on empty can lines. The stated mission is to provide excellent customer service through customized solutions.

name: CableLabs
old_description: As CableLabs matured, its leadership began thinking of expanding the impact of CableLabs technologies. Originally founded under the name NetworkFX, Kyrio became the conduit for bringing broadband, security, networking, and testing services to device manufacturers and businesses outside the traditional cable market. Today, Kyrio's state-of-the-art testing lab boasts 180 test benches, 175 racks of equipment, and over $120 million worth of investment, allowing companies to ensure their latest innovations are bug-free and ready for consumer use. Fun fact: Kyrio comes from the Greek word "kyrios" meaning "lord" or "master."
about:
CableLabs operates from Louisville, Colorado, where it was founded in 1988 as a non-profit research and development consortium funded by the global cable industry.

The lab conducts research and development across state-of-the-art facilities, develops industry specifications (including DOCSIS standards), manages patents and licensing, and fosters collaboration among cable operators, equipment manufacturers, and technology providers. Through its subsidiary Kyrio, CableLabs operates a testing and certification operation with more than 180 test benches, 175 equipment racks, and over $120 million in invested infrastructure, having certified more than 1,500 products to date. The organization holds over 800 granted patents spanning three decades.

CableLabs serves the broadband telecommunications sector, working directly with over 2,250 vendor companies and 22,000 individual members across the cable industry ecosystem. Its technologies underpin more than 550 million shipped devices based on its cable modem specifications, and its standards influence a $460 billion industry reaching over half a billion users daily.

The consortium was established to advance connectivity technologies for the benefit of the cable industry, focusing on secure delivery of high-speed data, video, voice, and next-generation services. By aligning government and industry priorities through technology policy work, CableLabs aims to promote innovation, facilitate trade, and strengthen competitiveness across the broadband landscape.

old_description: Cadence is the leading manufacturer of custom sharps solutions, enabling better outcomes for OEMs, surgeons, and patients. Our sharps solutions provide unique geometries for superior cutting or piercing.
about:
Cadence, Inc. is headquartered in DeLand, Florida. The company operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in medical devices and precision components for the MedTech and pharmaceutical industries.

Cadence provides vertically integrated contract manufacturing from complex components to finished devices. Its core capabilities include custom sharps (specialty blades and needles), plastics overmolding, insert molding, and injection molding; complex machining such as Swiss, screw, micro, PEEK, and LaserSwiss; precision metal stamping with microstamping, multi-slide, and reel-to-reel technology; deep draw forming; metal injection molding (MIM); and precision laser processing (welding, cutting, marking, drilling, ablation). The company runs certified ISO Class 7 and Class 8 cleanrooms at dedicated facilities in Cranberry Township, Pennsylvania, and Alajuela, Costa Rica, and operates FDA-registered, cGMP-compliant sites in Pennsylvania, Virginia, Costa Rica, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin. It also designs and builds custom automation equipment for assembly and inspection.

Cadence serves MedTech and Pharma original equipment manufacturers worldwide, supporting applications in medical devices, drug delivery systems, and diagnostics. Customers range from large multinational OEMs to early-stage innovators requiring design for manufacturability (DFM), design for assembly (DFA), prototyping, process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), and new product introduction (NPI) support.

The company emphasizes a single-source model that consolidates the supply chain, reduces time to market, and leverages external expertise. A dedicated sterilization management facility and comprehensive quality system (ISO 13485:2016, FDA 21 CFR Part 820) are cited as key differentiators for ensuring compliance and patient safety.

Calsak serves engineers, fabricators, procurement teams, and manufacturers across industries such as marine and boat building, architectural signage, construction, printing and graphics, aerospace, automotive, medical, retail display, data center, and advertising and art. Its materials are used for hulls, cabinetry, dock equipment, signage, cladding, glazing, printable substrates, data center containment panels, and medical device housings.

The company differentiates itself by combining global sourcing with domestic fulfillment, routing orders from the nearest branch to minimize lead times. Technical sales specialists provide material selection, compliance review, and specification guidance. Proprietary brands are developed for specific performance demands rather than repackaged commodity grades.

about:
CAM International, LLC is based in Smyrna, Tennessee. The company was founded in 1973 by James C. Van Slyke, who had worked in the automotive aftermarket since 1936. Recognizing a need for a more organized approach to handling stock lifts, changeovers, buybacks, and overstock inventories, Van Slyke established CAM International to reduce costs and disruption for manufacturers while providing accountability and equitable recovery. The business remains family-owned and operated, now led by third-generation president Matt Van Slyke.

CAM International operates as a redistributor and liquidator of genuine automotive aftermarket parts. The company purchases surplus inventory — including overruns, overstock, shelf-pulls, and packaging changes — from major manufacturers, warehouse distributors, and jobbers. Every piece is inspected, scanned, and packed at its facility, backed by a 30-day guarantee that parts are genuine (not reboxed or relabeled), currently cataloged, and in clean, salable condition. CAM describes itself as the oldest and largest aftermarket parts liquidator in the United States and Canada, with inventories spanning hundreds of brands and thousands of product lines.

The company serves automotive aftermarket manufacturers, warehouse distributors, and jobbers. Manufacturers use CAM’s stock-lift and changeover programs to minimize displacement expense and maximize recovery on competitive inventory. Distributors and jobbers turn to CAM to liquidate single product lines or entire operations, and to purchase discounted inventory at 20–70% off normal cost. CAM also handles heavy-duty parts stock lifts.

CAM International was started to bring accountability and equitable recovery to the stock-lift process, enabling warehouse distributors and jobbers to be more profitable and competitive. Its differentiators include a family-owned, third-generation leadership structure, a 3-way 30-day guarantee on every purchase, and specialization in manufacturer stock-lift and changeover programs.

about:
Carolina Wood Products operates from Marshville, North Carolina, where it has manufactured wood pallets and packaging since 1969. The company was founded by Robert and Frances Horne in nearby Peachland before moving to its current Marshville facility. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the business is led by Ronald and Randy Horne, with the next generation, Matt and Randall Horne, recently completing a major sawmill expansion.

The company supplies pallets and packaging to businesses in Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, Fayetteville, Durham, and throughout the Piedmont and coastal regions.

Carolina Wood Products emphasizes that it is a local manufacturer, not a broker, with every pallet built on-site in Marshville. This vertical integration allows consistent quality, faster turnaround, and direct communication with the production team. The family ownership and recent capital investment reflect a long-term commitment to the region’s supply chain.

name: Cavist
old_description: Overmolding electronic assemblies yields protection against the harshest environments. Our primary goal is to determine the absolute best way to encapsulate your cable, connector or PCBA, and scale that into volume manufacturing here at Cavist.
about:
Cavist was incorporated in Reno, Nevada, in 1998 by Danish-born founders Kurt Carlson and Reimer Hansen to bring European low-pressure molding technology to the United States. The company began as an equipment developer, introducing the MoldMan line of low-pressure molding machines, before launching a contract manufacturing division in 2008. In 2023, after 26 years of growth, Cavist transitioned to 100% employee ownership.

Today Cavist operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in encapsulating and protecting electronic assemblies. Its core processes include low-pressure molding (LPM), 2-shot overmolding, epoxy overmolding, and cable assembly overmolding, supplemented by turnkey supply services that cover procurement, assembly, testing, and packaging. The 30,000-square-foot facility houses more than 25 injection molding machines and a staff of 35-plus engineers, technicians, and support personnel. Quality systems are certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016, and the site includes ISO Class 8 cleanrooms for medical device work.

The company serves automotive, medical, wearable, and defense markets, with customers ranging from individual inventors to Fortune 500 corporations. Automotive programs include sealing for EV and under-hood electronics; medical projects cover implantable and wearable devices requiring biocompatible materials; defense work addresses ruggedized connectors and cable assemblies for harsh environments.

Cavist differentiates itself through 25-plus years of dedicated low-pressure molding experience, in-house moldflow simulation that validates gating and fill before production, and engineering support that begins at the design stage with DFM, material selection, and prototyping. The employee-owned structure is intended to ensure long-term stability and accountability from prototype through high-volume runs.

name: Center for Composite Materials (CCM)
old_description: The Center for Composite Materials is an internationally recognized Center of Excellence for interdisciplinary research, education, and technology transfer in the areas of materials and synthesis, multifunctional materials, processing science, mechanics and design, sensing and control, and simulation.
about:
The Center for Composite Materials (CCM) was established in 1974 at the University of Delaware in Newark, Delaware. As a university-based research center, it operates under the College of Engineering and draws faculty from multiple departments including mechanical engineering, materials science, and chemical engineering. The center was created to advance interdisciplinary research in composite materials and has since been designated a Center of Excellence eight times by the National Science Foundation and the Department of Defense.

CCM provides a full spectrum of composites research and development services, from material characterization and mechanical testing to process development, prototyping, and component validation. Its 53,688-square-foot facility houses equipment valued at more than $25 million, including autoclaves, resin infusion systems, automated fiber placement, additive manufacturing platforms, and a suite of thermal, mechanical, and nondestructive evaluation instruments. In a recent year, more than 51 faculty members, 41 research professionals and postdoctoral fellows, and 71 graduate and undergraduate students participated in over 50 research projects with annual expenditures exceeding $17 million.

The center serves the automotive, aerospace, defense, and energy sectors. It maintains long-standing collaborations with government agencies such as the Department of Energy, NASA, DARPA, and the U.S. Army’s TARDEC, as well as with industry partners including BAE Systems, major OEMs, and Tier‑1 suppliers. More than 350 companies, ranging from startups to Fortune 500 firms, have engaged with CCM through its University‑Industry Consortium.

CCM distinguishes itself through end-to-end integration of materials science, process engineering, and validation under one roof, enabling rapid translation of laboratory discoveries into manufacturable solutions. Its mission emphasizes technology transfer, workforce development, and the creation of predictive modeling tools that link atomistic physics to composite performance.

about:
Crescent Textile Solutions operates from Two Rivers, Wisconsin, on the western shore of Lake Michigan. The business traces its roots to 1923 when Archibald and Theodore Webster, sons of William Walter Webster, acquired an existing knitting mill and renamed it Crescent Woolen Mills. The Webster family’s textile lineage begins earlier, with Matthew Webster emigrating from England in 1855 and establishing woolen mills in Minnesota. DairyChem is headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, and has been manufacturing natural dairy flavors since 1933. DairyChem later acquired Chumlea's laboratory and expanded its capabilities and product portfolio.

Today, DairyChem produces dairy concentrates, natural flavors, and clean-label solutions in a modern manufacturing plant. Its core processes include fermentation, steam distillation, and natural enzyme modification of milk, butter, and cheese. The company also offers blended and compounded flavor systems in liquid, paste, or spray-dried powder forms. Two divisions extend its reach: Ingretec, a sister company specializing in cheese flavorings and fillings that are two to six times stronger than conventional cheese, and FLVRtec, a subsidiary creating natural, allergen-free liquid flavors for savory, sweet, and emerging categories.

DairyChem serves food and beverage manufacturers across applications such as sauces, fillings, soups, spreads, dips, dressings, processed cheese, and dairy alternatives.

As a family-owned, independent business, DairyChem emphasizes long-term partnership, short lead times, custom packaging, and flexible ordering. Its R&D team combines deep dairy expertise with modern food science to deliver stable, versatile flavors that perform in real-world processing conditions.

about:
DeWys Manufacturing began in 1977 when Mark DeWys started the company in a small red barn on his parents’ property in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Drawing on experience from his grandfather’s tool-and-die shop, Mark initially produced tubular fireplace inserts and small metal parts. The business relocated to its current Marne, Michigan facility in 1986, and Mark’s brother Jon DeWys joined in 1987, later assuming leadership after Mark’s passing in 1999. The company remains family-owned.

Today DeWys operates as DeWys Metal Solutions, a full-service contract metal manufacturer offering OEM precision sheet metal fabrication, forming and bending, laser cutting, turret punching, robotic and manual welding, machining, powder coating, product development, assembly, and contract manufacturing. The organization comprises six specialized brands—DeWys Manufacturing, DeWys Stainless Solutions, Wyze Designs, ReFab, Shoreline Powder Coating, and American Grower Resource—serving over 160 customers from a campus at 15300 8th Avenue in Marne. The company highlights its use of a fully automated part-sorting robot for laser cutting, noted as the second such installation in the United States.

The company serves industries including medical equipment, food and beverage, agriculture, renewable energy, data centers, retail fixtures, office furniture, fixed seating, material handling, heavy-duty equipment, electrical equipment, and EV charging. Customers range from OEMs requiring precision components to firms seeking complete contract manufacturing solutions.

DeWys emphasizes its family-owned, American-made identity, lean manufacturing principles, and workforce development through DeWys University, established in 2012. The firm has earned recognition on the Fabricator’s FAB 40 list, multiple Best & Brightest workplace awards, and the MMA Small Tier Manufacturer Award.

old_description: We solve challenges. If you’re struggling with nonconforming parts we’re here to resolve your issues. about:
EnTech Plastics, Inc. operates from a 45,000-square-foot facility in Corry, Pennsylvania. Founded in 1996, the company has built its reputation on solving difficult molding challenges that other suppliers cannot.

The shop specializes in low- to mid-volume custom injection molding on machines ranging from 44 to 1,100 tons, producing parts from 1 gram up to 22 pounds. Core processes include gas-assist, insert molding, over molding, and master unit die (MUD) frames, supported by closed-loop controllers, SPC monitoring, and real-time production tracking. The facility dedicates 25,000 square feet to manufacturing and 20,000 square feet to warehousing with nine loading docks. Engineering services cover design for manufacturability, tool building, resin selection (including high-temperature grades such as PEI, PPS, and PEEK), and full assembly.

Customers span heavy-duty truck, medical, industrial, and consumer markets. EnTech has produced large components such as truck body panels, medical device housings, industrial machinery covers, and consumer product parts. Long-term clients include ANDRITZ Pulp & Paper and other OEMs that moved work to EnTech after experiencing inconsistent quality from larger molders.

The company positions itself on the intersection of low volume and high tonnage—a combination that is rare in the industry—and on delivering parts that are both aesthetically precise and mechanically robust. Its stated differentiator is the willingness to take on problematic tooling or nonconforming parts, diagnose root causes, and re-engineer the process to achieve consistent output.

about:
Genovac Antibody Discovery operates from its headquarters in Fargo, North Dakota, with additional antibody discovery operations in Freiburg, Germany. The company traces its origins to 1999 when three University of Freiburg professors launched the venture based on the institution’s pioneering antibody research. In 2020, a management-led buyout of Aldevron’s antibody discovery business unit relaunched Genovac under its current structure.

The firm specializes in end-to-end antibody discovery and production against challenging targets such as ion channels and GPCRs. Its platform combines genetic immunization, multiple host species, and several single B cell screening technologies—including the Berkeley Lights Beacon instrument—alongside biologics production and a full suite of characterization services. Genovac reports more than 3,600 completed antibody discovery projects and 25 years of cumulative experience.

George's Furniture is a second-generation family-owned business located in Marietta, Pennsylvania, operating from a farm location just outside historic Maytown since 1975. The company was founded in 1970 by George Martin as George's Woodcrafts, stemming from his early interest in woodworking and a rocking chair design he created at age 10. In 2008, George retired and passed the business to his daughter Juanita and son-in-law Chris Horst, who continue the tradition.

The workshop produces custom handcrafted Amish furniture using 100% solid hardwood—walnut, cherry, oak, and hard maple—with no plywood, particle board, or veneers. Each piece is built by a single craftsman from lumber selection through final finishing, signed and dated for authenticity. The process includes design consultation, customization of dimensions, finish, and details, and handcrafted construction. Typical lead time is 2-3 months. The company sells direct to customers, eliminating middleman markup.

The company serves residential customers seeking heirloom-quality furniture for homes, including tables, chairs, benches, and extension tables. Examples include a customer from Brookeville, MD who purchased a table, chairs, and bench.

The business was started to address frustration with poor-quality furniture; George Martin's rocking chair innovation reflected a focus on durability and safety. The company differentiates itself through traditional Amish woodworking techniques, a year-long apprenticeship for craftsmen, direct-to-customer sales, and a lifetime value proposition.

about:
Griffin Foods is headquartered in Muskogee, Oklahoma, where it was founded in 1908 by brothers John T. and Charles M. Griffin. The company began as the Griffin Grocery Company in McAlester before moving to Muskogee in 1923, when John Griffin built a three-story facility housing administration, warehousing, and processing. Now a fourth-generation, family-owned and minority-owned business, it operates under the Griffin Holding Company alongside Griffin Communications.

The company specializes in manufacturing and packaging liquid and emulsified semi-solid food products, with core lines in table syrups, mustards, molasses, imitation vanilla, and corn syrups. Through its 2006 acquisition of House of Webster in Rogers, Arkansas, Griffin added gourmet jams, jellies, preserves, fruit butters, relishes, salsas, barbecue sauces, salad dressings, and pickled products. It offers co-packing and private-label services, formulating new products or running customer formulas, and packages in retail, foodservice, and industrial sizes. The Muskogee facility serves distribution across the continental U.S., Mexico, and Europe; by 2000 the company employed roughly 100 people and recorded several million dollars in annual sales.

Griffin supplies food manufacturers, foodservice distributors, and retail grocery chains, with its branded products stocked in most Oklahoma-area supermarkets. Major customers receive branded, private-label, and co-packed items, and the company sells direct by the case.

Griffin differentiates itself through food-safety certifications—SQF Food Safety Code for Food Manufacturing and Kosher Parve certification from the Orthodox Union—and a commitment to allergen-free production (no Big 8 allergens). The company emphasizes quick response, high-grade ingredients, and a track record of customer-service awards.

The U.S. entity was established in 2013 to support the company's expanding footprint in the Americas.

The company designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of solar inverters ranging from 0.75 kW to 253 kW, lithium-ion battery storage systems for residential and commercial use, EV chargers (3–22 kW AC and 20/40 kW DC), and cloud-based monitoring hardware and software. Globally, the organization employs over 1,000 people and reports more than 6 million end users connected to its cloud platform across 190-plus countries.

Growatt's solutions target residential, commercial, utility-scale, and transportation sectors. Its customer base includes solar installers, engineering-procurement-construction (EPC) firms, distributors, and end-users. about:
Gulfstream Steel & Supply was founded in 1990 in Holly Ridge, North Carolina, as a locally owned and operated metals service center. The company began as a dependable source of metal materials and services for the eastern North Carolina region.

The company maintains an extensive inventory of carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized steel, and PVC pipe and fittings, and provides a range of value‑added processing services. Its capabilities include structural sawing, mitre and CNC cutting, plate burning and beveling up to 14‑inch thickness, CNC machining on HAAS VF9 and VF4 mills and a Quickmill gantry center, sheet and coil shearing, forming, and punching, as well as pipe and tube cutting, drilling, and slotting. An on‑site blast shop prepares surfaces with black beauty and steel shot media, and a dedicated hose shop assembles custom hydraulic and pneumatic hose assemblies. Gulfstream also operates a fleet of 24‑foot Freightliners, a 28‑foot tandem‑axle International, and a 53‑foot Volvo for delivery across southeastern North Carolina.

Gulfstream serves industrial, agricultural, manufacturing, MRO, and construction customers, with a particular focus on U.S. military installations, law‑enforcement agencies, first‑responder units, and K‑9 training facilities. The company has worked with prime vendors such as Darley Defense on training‑solution projects.

The business emphasizes local hiring, including veterans, and promotes next‑day delivery on most stock items with free local delivery on orders over $500. Its differentiation rests on a large regional inventory, in‑house processing equipment, and a commitment to coastal‑environment durability through quality control and corrosion‑resistant coatings.

name: Gus Willy Apparel
old_description: Our professional grade embroidery machines support 21 work stations.  The Gus Willy embroidery team has over 50 years experience and can put your logo on anything from polos, caps, pullovers and more.  We can even make your design pop with our 3D embroidery capabilities.
about:
Gus Willy Apparel was founded in 2017 in Metairie, Louisiana, by Craig Leaumont, who named the business after his third child, Gustave William Leaumont, known as Gus Willy. The company began as a custom apparel operation focused on screen printing and embroidery for teams and corporate clients.

Today the shop runs two automatic and four manual screen‑print presses alongside professional‑grade embroidery machines with 21 work stations, including 3D embroidery capability. An in‑house graphic design team prepares artwork for both decoration methods. Beyond apparel, the company supplies promotional items such as pens, koozies, water bottles, and custom etched tumblers, and has expanded into a full‑line safety distributor offering ANSI‑compliant high‑visibility vests, jackets, hard hats, helmets, gloves, and other job‑site essentials. Orders range from small crew outfitting to workforces of several hundred.

The customer base spans construction, manufacturing, utilities, oil and gas, youth sports leagues, and corporate accounts across the southeastern United States.
